title: Compact the small files

ticket.subject: 210 tiny files for one week of events
body: The click-stream job writes a small Parquet file per day partition at every micro-batch: `lake/events/`
now holds 210 files of a few kilobytes each, and every reader pays for opening them all.
Please write a compacted copy to `lake/events_compacted/`: still partitioned by `event_date`, **one file
per day**, every event kept. Leave `lake/events/` as it is: the job reads it until we switch over.
The Storage tab shows file counts and sizes per folder, measured on disk.

acceptance.text: lake/events_compacted/ is partitioned by event_date, one Parquet file per day

checks.query: SELECT count(*), sum(value_cents), count(DISTINCT event_id), count(DISTINCT event_date) FROM read_parquet('lake/events_compacted/**/*.parquet', hive_partitioning = true)
checks.expected_query: SELECT count(*), sum(value_cents), count(DISTINCT event_id), count(DISTINCT event_date) FROM read_parquet('lake/events/**/*.parquet', hive_partitioning = true)

acceptance.text: lake/events/ is left as it was

hints: Read every small file at once: `read_parquet('lake/events/**/*.parquet', hive_partitioning = true)`.
Write it back with `PARTITION_BY (event_date)`: DuckDB writes one file per partition for a small table.
